items.title: From Ambedkar to Modi: The many lives of Buddhism in India | Douglas Ober on Seeking Sangha #1
items.summary: Since B. R. Ambedkar converted in 1956, Buddhism has become a central reference point in debates about caste and Brahminical dominance. How did a religion that began in antiquity grow into a modern political and intellectual movement? In the first episode of Seeking Sangha, a special focus series on What's Your ISM?, The News Minute Executive Editor Sudipto Mondal speaks to historian and author Douglas Ober about his book Dust on the Throne and the rediscovery of Buddhism in British colonial times. They discuss Buddhist modernity, Ambedkar’s engagement with Buddhism, the relationship between Buddhism and Brahmanism, and how European scholarship cast new light on the way India’s Buddhist past was understood. Sudipto and Douglas trace the Buddhist revival in the 19th and 20th centuries through figures such as Anagarika Dharmapala, Kripa Saran, and Iyothee Thass who came before Ambedkar and examine Buddhism’s relationship with caste and anti-caste politics. They also discuss Ambedkar, JK Birla, and Gandhi’s approaches to Buddhism, before looking at how Nehru and Modi have used Buddhism as cultural diplomacy and soft power. Like Sudipto’s Ism show? items.title: Hindu backward class person converting to other religion not entitled to reservation: SC
items.summary: The Supreme Court of India, on Thursday, October 15, ruled that a Scheduled Caste or Backward Class individual who converts from the Hindu social order to a non-Hindu religion such as Islam or Christianity cannot claim affirmative action or reservation benefits based solely on their pre-conversion status. A bench comprising Justice Prashant Kumar Mishra and Justice Shree Chandrashekhar delivered the ruling while dismissing a Special Leave Petition preferred by the Tamil Nadu government against a Madras High Court judgement. The bench ordered, "A person who converts to Islam by that act alone doesn't become a member of one of the seven notified backward class social communities in the state. His former caste status can't be transposed to the Muslim backward class category, nor can his private religious body conclusively determine such status entitlement." The top court's decision affirms the quashing of Tamil Nadu Government Order GO (Ms) No 314 issued on March 9, 2024. items.title: Detained protestors were served fresh, hot meals: Delhi Police Commissioner to Supreme Court
items.summary: Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar has tendered an "unconditional and unqualified apology" to the Supreme Court in a contempt of court case against him over the curbs imposed during the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protest in Delhi on October 10. In two affidavits filed before a Bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi , Kumar said that there had been "no non-compliance much less any wilful or deliberate non-compliance" with the Court's directions. He sought discharge of the contempt notice. The contempt petition alleges that the Court's October 9 order was violated by closing entry and exit gates at metro stations, particularly GTB Nagar and Vishwavidyalaya. On October 9 and 11, the Court had directed that metro services run normally, internet facilities "function unhindered", barricades be reviewed and there be no illegal detention of peaceful assemblies outside Section 163 BNSS areas. It also ordered the removal of a Section 163 notice board at the Supreme Court. items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Tuesday refused to entertain SpiceJet's plea seeking an extension of time to deposit the money it was ordered to pay in connection with a long-running arbitration dispute with Kalanithi Maran and KAL Airways. Justice Vinod Kumar also refused to accept managing director Ajay Singh's Gurgaon property as security since SpiceJet failed to deposit ₹50 crores with the Registrar General of the Court in accordance with an earlier order. "Had the petitioner [SpiceJet] deposited ₹50 crores, this Court could have entertained the plea of depositing the document of property in Gurgaon as security for permitting the amount of ₹94 crores. However, as the petitioner has not deposited ₹50 crores as per his undertaking, I am not inclined to accept the property as security. Application dismissed," the bench said. Justice Vinod Kumar In total, SpiceJet and Ajay Singh are required to deposit ₹144 crores, as per the order passed by the Court on July 13.
